alignments.note: Jussive rendered as the bare optative Grant.
Dative לְ rendered as a bare English indirect object (rule 40).
Suffix on the silenced dative takes thee (rule 40).

The ASV recasts כִלְבָבֶךָ 'according to thy heart' as 'thy heart's desire': heart's is the noun's own word and thy the suffix's, and desire is what the ASV spends on the conformity relation the כְּ carries — drop desire and only that relation is lost, exactly as dropping the כְּ from the Hebrew leaves 'give thee thy heart'. Rule 40 silences a preposition only where the ASV spends nothing on its contribution, and rule 24 heads a preposition recast as a phrase writing none of its own lexeme on the content word the phrase turns on. The competing reading marks the כְּ unrepresented and desire added; a fusion of כְּ with the noun was also considered and rejected because heart's is the noun's own word (rule 30).
Noun rendered as the English possessive heart's.

review_notes: Corrected: desire is given to the comparative כְּ as the ASV's rendering of the 'according to' relation rather than left added beside an unrepresented preposition; the competing reading is named in the unit note.
